note: Every factual statement the game shows. category: archive (from a NASA or PDS page in the source register), game_time (time made shorter for play), fiction (made up for the game), balance (game tuning, no source). lead_ids are search leads that were not opened; they are never shown as citations.

claims.title: Gravity on Mars
claims.text: Gravity on Mars is 3.73 m/s². Things fall more slowly than on Earth, so you can jump higher.
claims.note: Mean surface gravity from the NASA Mars Fact Sheet. The game uses this value for walking and jumping.

claims.title: How long a Mars day is
claims.text: A day on Mars is called a sol. One sol lasts 24 h 39 min 35 s, a little longer than a day on Earth.
claims.note: Mean solar day 24 h 39 min 35.244 s (Mars24 technical notes). Rounded to whole seconds here.

claims.title: Sols go faster in the game
claims.text: In the game, one sol lasts 20 real minutes, so you can see day and night pass while you play.
claims.note: 20 minutes is the default. The host can choose 5 to 120 minutes. It is a game-time control, not the length of a real Mars day.

claims.title: Oxygen from water
claims.text: On the International Space Station, a machine splits water into oxygen and hydrogen. This is called electrolysis.
claims.note: ISS evidence, not Mars evidence. The colony's life support copies this idea.

claims.title: Oxygen from Mars air
claims.text: A small test machine called MOXIE made oxygen from the carbon dioxide in Mars air. It made 122 g of oxygen in 16 runs.
claims.note: Best rate 12 g per hour, purity 98% or better. A small technology test on Mars.

claims.title: The colony's big oxygen machines
claims.text: The colony's oxygen machines are much bigger than MOXIE. That bigger machine is made up for the game.
claims.note: Fictional 2080 scale-up of the MOXIE idea.

claims.title: Water is recycled
claims.text: The space station cleans and reuses about 90 percent of its water.
claims.note: Water recovery about 90 percent on the ISS. The game's own recycling share is game balance.

claims.title: Plants grown in space
claims.text: Astronauts have grown lettuce, Chinese cabbage, mizuna mustard, red Russian kale and zinnia flowers on the space station.
claims.note: Crops grown in the Veggie chamber on the ISS. Growing plants on the ISS does not prove farming on Mars.

claims.title: What Mars air is made of
claims.text: Mars air is mostly carbon dioxide: 95.1% by volume. It has only 0.16% oxygen, far too little to breathe.
claims.note: Atmosphere by volume from the NASA Mars Fact Sheet: CO2 95.1%, N2 2.59%, Ar 1.94%, O2 0.16%, CO 0.06%.

claims.title: How cold Mars is
claims.text: The average temperature on Mars is about −59 °C.
claims.note: About 214 K (−59 °C), a global average from the NASA Mars Fact Sheet. Not local weather.

claims.title: Sunlight at Mars
claims.text: At Mars, sunlight brings 586.2 W of power to each square metre facing the Sun.
claims.note: Solar irradiance 586.2 W/m² from the NASA Mars Fact Sheet. This is sunlight, not what a solar panel makes.

claims.title: Dust and solar power
claims.text: Dust on solar panels and in the air lowers how much electricity the panels make.
claims.note: Source not yet checked. S18 (InSight dust news) is a search lead only; the page was not opened.

claims.title: Radio messages to Earth take time
claims.text: Radio messages between Mars and Earth take several minutes to arrive.
claims.note: Source not yet checked. S15 pages give different ranges and were not opened, so the game shows no number.

claims.title: How fast the crew uses supplies
claims.text: How much oxygen, water and food each crew member uses in the game is game balance. These numbers were chosen for play, not measured.
claims.note: GameBalance rates per active crew member. No source.

claims.title: Battery, solar and room power numbers
claims.text: The battery size, the solar power and the power each room uses are game balance numbers, not real ones.
claims.note: GameBalance values in kWh and kW. No source.

claims.title: The colony is made up
claims.text: The colony, its crew and its 2080 machines are made up for the game. No colony like it exists on Mars today.
claims.note: The fictional colony and its equipment. Real places such as Gale crater and Jezero crater are not the colony's site.
